annotations.title: Grace to you and peace.
annotations.text: [1] It is a kind of bleſſing rather then a prophane ſalutation, proper to the Apoſtles, of greater vertue then the benedictions of the fathers in the old Teſtament. The holy fathers of the Church ſeemed to abſteine from it for their reuerence to the Apoſtles. [2] The Manichees (Auguſt. cont. ep. funda. c. 5. 6.) and other Heretikes [3] (as alſo theſe of our time) becauſe they vvould be counted Apoſtles, often vſe it.

annotations.title: Your faith renoumed.
annotations.text: [1] The holy Doctors vpon theſe words of the Apoſtle, and ſpecially by our Maſter's promiſe [2] made to Peter, that his faith ſhould not faile, giue great teſtimonie for the prouidence of God in the preſeruation of the Roman faith. S. Cyprian thus: ep. 55. nu. 6. They are ſo bold to cary letters from profane Schiſmatics to the chaire of Peter and the principal Church whence Prieſtly vnitie roſe: not conſidering the Romans to be them whoſe faith (the Apoſtle being the commender) was praiſed, to whom miſbelief cannot haue acceſſe. So S. Hierom Apolog. adu. Ruff. li. 3. c. 4. to. 2. [3] know you, that the Roman faith commended by the Apoſtle's mouth, will receiue no ſuch deceits, nor can be poſſibly changed, though an Angel taught othervviſe, being fenced by S. Paul's authoritie. Againe ep. 63. ad Pammach. & Oceanum. c. 4. to. 2. Whatſoeuer thou be that auoucheſt new ſects, I pray thee haue reſpect to the Roman ears. Spare the faith which was praiſed by the Apoſtles voice. And in another place [4]: Will ye know, o Paula and Euſtochium, hovv the Apoſtle hath noted euery prouince vvith their proprieties? The faith of the people of Rome is praiſed. Where is there ſo great concourſe to Churches and Martyrs' ſepulchres? [5] Where ſoundeth Amen like thunder from heauen, or where are the temples (void of Idols) ſo ſhaken as there? Not that the Romans haue another faith then the reſt of the Chriſtian Churches, but that there is in them more deuotion and ſimplicitie of faith. In another place the ſame holy Doctor ſignifieth that it is all one to ſay, the Roman faith, and the Catholic. Apolog. 1. adu. Ruff. c. 1. So doth S. Cyprian ep. 52. num. 1. ad Antonianum: and S. Ambroſe de obitu fratris, in med. [6] Whereupon, this vvord, Roman, is added to, Catholic, in many countries where ſects do abound, for the better diſtinction of true believers from Heretics: which in all ages did hate and abhorre the Roman faith and Church, as all malefactors do their Iudges and correctors.

notes.text: It can not faile, nor be corrupted.
Prooem. li. 2. Com. in ep. ad Gal.
The Romane stations, a token of greater faith and deuotion.
The Catholike and Romane faith al one.

annotations.title: Serue in ſpirit.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> Diuerſe Heretikes when they heare that God is a ſpirit, and muſt be ſerued and adored in ſpirit, imagine, that he muſt be honoured only invvardly, vvithout ceremonies and external workes: vvhich you ſee is othervviſe, for that the Apoſtle ſerued God in ſpirit, by preaching the Goſpel. To ſerue God then in ſpirit, is to ſerue him with faith, hope, and charitie, and vvith al workes proceding of them: as to ſerue him carnally, is, vvith vvorkes external, vvithout the ſaid internal vertues.

notes.text: How God is serued in spirit.

annotations.title: A memorie of you.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> A great example of charitie for al men, ſpecially for Prelates and Paſtors, not only to preach, but to pray continually for the conuerſion of people to Chriſtes faith: vvhich the Apoſtle did for them vvhom he neuer knew, in reſpect of Gods honour only and the zeale of ſoules.

annotations.title: To euangelize.
annotations.text: <mn>[1]</mn> The Goſpel is not only the life of our Sauiour written by the foure Euangeliſtes, nor only that vvhich is written in the nevv Teſtament: but their vvhole courſe of preaching and teaching the faith. Vvhich faith commeth ordinarily of preaching and hearing, and not of writing or reading. And therfore S. Paul thought not him ſelf diſcharged by writing to the Romanes, but his deſire vvas to preach vnto them: for that was the proper commiſſion giuen to the Apoſtles, <mn>[2]</mn> to preach to al nations. <mn>[3]</mn> The writing of the bookes of the Teſtament, is an other part of Gods prouidence, neceſſary for the Church in general, but not neceſſarie for euery man in particular: as to be taught and preached vnto, is for euery one of age and vnderſtanding. And therfore S. Peter (vvho was the cheefe of the Commiſſion) wrote litle: many of them wrote nothing at al: and S. Paul that wrote moſt, vvrote but litle in compariſon of his preaching: nor to any but ſuch as were conuerted to the faith by preaching before.

notes.text: The Gospel is not only the Written Word.
The Apostles vvriting, and preaching, whether more necessarie, and how.

annotations.title: Liueth by faith.
annotations.text: In the 10. to the Hebrewes, he ſheweth by this place of the Prophete (Abacuc 2) that the iuſt though he liue here in peregrination, and ſeeth not preſently nor enioyeth the life euerlaſting promiſed to him, yet holdeth faſt the hope thereof by faith. In this place he applieth the Prophetes wordes further to this ſenſe, That it is our faith, that is to ſay, ◦ the Catholike beleefe (ſaith S. Auguſtine li. 3 cont. 2 ep. Pelag.) which maketh a iuſt man, and diſtinguiſheth betwene the iuſt and vniuſt, and that by the law of faith, and not by the lavv of workes. Whereof it riſeth, that the Iew, the Heathen Philoſopher, and the Heretike, though they excelled in al vvorkes of moral vertues, could not yet be iuſt: and a Catholike Chriſtian man liuing but an ordinarie honeſt life, either not ſinning greatly, or ſupplying his faults by penance, is iuſt. And this difference riſeth by faith. not that faith can ſaue any man without vvorkes, For it is not a reprobate faith that we ſpeake of, (as the holy Doctor ſaith) but that vvhich worketh by charitie, and therfore remitteth ſinnes and maketh one iuſt. See S. Auguſtines place.

notes.text: The Catholike or Christian faith with good workes iustifieth. & without this faith, no workes whatsoeuer.

annotations.title: Is reuealed.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> By al the paſſage folowing you may ſee, that the Goſpel and Chriſts law conſiſteth not only in preaching faith, (though that be the ground, and is firſt alwaies to be done:) but to teach vertuous life and good vvorkes, and to denounce damnation to al them that commit deadly ſinnes and repent not. And againe we ſee that not only lacke of faith is a ſinne, but al other actes done againſt Gods commaundements.

annotations.title: Hath deliuered them up.
annotations.text: <mn>[1]</mn> As he ſaith here, God deliuered them up, ſo to the Epheſians (c. 4, 19.) he ſaith of the ſame perſons and things, They deliuered themſelves up to all vncleanneſſe. So that it is not meant here that God doth driue, force, or cauſe any man to ſinne, as diuers blaſphemous Heretics do hold: but only that by his juſt iudgement, for their owne deſeruing, <mn>[2]</mn> and for due puniſhment of their former grievous offences, he vvithholdeth his grace from them, and ſo ſuffereth them to fall further into other ſins. As, for their crime of Idolatrie, to ſuffer them to fall into vnnatural abominations: as now for hereſie, he taketh his grace and mercie from many, and ſo they fall headlong into all kind of turpitude, as contrarywiſe, for ill life, he ſuffereth many to fall into hereſie. And for Chriſt's ſake let euery one that is entangled with the Idolatrie of this time, that is to ſay, vvith theſe nevv ſects, looke vvel into his owne conſcience, whether his forſaking the true God, may not come vnto him for a puniſhment of his former or preſent ill life which he liueth.

notes.text: God is not the author of sin.
God punisheth sin by permitting men to fall further and further.

annotations.title: Worthy of death.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> Here you ſee vvhy the Church taketh ſome ſinnes to be deadly, and calleth them mortal: to vvit, becauſe al that doe them, are worthie of damnation: others be venial, that is to ſay, pardonable of their owne nature and not worthy of damnation.
